sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: National & International Days (राष्ट्रीय एवं अंतर्राष्ट्रीय दिवस) representing historical events, global awareness themes, and cultural milestones.
Observed throughout the calendar year from **January 1** to **December 31**.
Observed globally (**United Nations** bodies) and nationally across India.
Declared by the **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)**, **WHO**, **UNESCO**, and the **Government of India**.
Crucial static General Awareness topic for **UPSSSC PET**; frequently asked in 1-2 direct questions.
Associated with specific yearly themes, official logos, global campaigns, and historical anniversaries.
High-yield scoring area covering recurring dates like **Yoga Day**, **Environment Day**, and **Women's Day**.
Includes newly added national days like **National Space Day** (**August 23**) and **Veer Baal Diwas** (**December 26**).

items.title: January to March: Health & Rights
items.content:
• **January 9:** Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (Return of **Mahatma Gandhi** from South Africa in **1915**)
• **January 12:** National Youth Day (**Swami Vivekananda** birth anniversary)
• **January 25:** National Voters Day & National Tourism Day
• **February 4:** World Cancer Day (**Close the Care Gap**)
• **March 8:** International Women's Day
• **March 22:** World Water Day
• **Mnemonic for Jan Days:** **'Pravasi Youth Vote on Tourism'** (9, 12, 25)

items.title: April to June: Environment & Health Focus
items.content:
• **April 7:** World Health Day (Establishment of **WHO** in **1948**)
• **April 22:** World Earth Day (**Invest In Our Planet**)
• **May 1:** International Labour Day (May Day)
• **May 31:** World No Tobacco Day
• **June 5:** World Environment Day (Established by **UNEP** in **1972**)
• **June 21:** International Day of Yoga (Proposed by PM **Narendra Modi**, started in **2015**)
• **Mnemonic for June Days:** **'Environment gives Yoga'** (5 and 21)

items.title: July to September: Population, Literacy & Peace
items.content:
• **July 11:** World Population Day
• **August 12:** International Youth Day & National Youth Day (**January 12**)
• **August 15:** Independence Day of India (**1947**)
• **August 29:** National Sports Day (**Major Dhyan Chand** birth anniversary)
• **September 5:** National Teachers Day (**Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan** birth anniversary)
• **September 8:** International Literacy Day
• **September 16:** World Ozone Day (**Montreal Protocol** signed in **1987**)

items.title: October to December: Gandhi, Children & Constitution
items.content:
• **October 2:** International Day of Non-Violence & **Gandhi Jayanti**
• **October 16:** World Food Day (Establishment of **FAO** in **1945**)
• **October 24:** United Nations Day (Creation of **UN** in **1945**)
• **November 14:** Children's Day (**Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru** birth anniversary) & World Diabetes Day
• **November 26:** Constitution Day of India (Adopted in **1949**) & National Law Day
• **December 1:** World AIDS Day
• **December 10:** Human Rights Day (Universal Declaration of Human Rights in **1948**)
• **December 23:** Kisan Diwas / Farmers Day (**Chaudhary Charan Singh** birth anniversary)
• **December 25:** Good Governance Day (**Atal Bihari Vajpayee** birth anniversary)
• **December 26:** Veer Baal Diwas (In honor of the martyrdom of Guru Gobind Singh's sons)

items.title: Special Newly Added National Days for UPSSSC PET
items.content:
• **August 23:** National Space Day (Commemorating successful landing of **Chandrayaan-3** on Moon)
• **August 7:** National Javelin Throw Day (Commemorating **Neeraj Chopra** Olympic Gold)
• **October 5:** National Dolphin Day
• **November 15:** Janajatiya Gaurav Divas (Birth anniversary of **Birsa Munda**)
• **Mnemonic for New Days:** **'Space Javelin Dolphin Tribe'** (Aug 23, Aug 7, Oct 5, Nov 15)

items.definition: March is Water (**March 22**), April is Earth (**April 22**), June is Environment (**June 5**), and September is Ozone (**September 16**). Remember sequence: **Water -> Earth -> Environment -> Ozone**.
**National Youth Day** is in **January** (12th - Vivekananda), while **International Youth Day** is in **August** (12th). Month difference only!
**October 2** is Gandhi Jayanti, which is universally celebrated as the **International Day of Non-Violence** declared by the UN.

items.term: Trick 4: Teachers Day vs World Teachers Day
items.definition: National Teachers Day is **September 5** (India). World Teachers Day is exactly one month later on **October 5**.
End of year has **December 23** (Farmers), **December 25** (Good Governance), and **December 26** (Veer Baal Diwas). Sequential block of three important national commemorations.

items.term: Trick 6: Constitution Day vs Republic Day
items.definition: Constitution Day is **November 26** (Adopted in 1949). Republic Day is **January 26** (Came into effect in 1950).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing National & International Youth Day
items.definition: Students often mix up January 12 (National) and August 12 (International). Both fall on the 12th day of their respective months.
National Teachers Day is September 5, but World Teachers Day is October 5. UPSSSC PET often tests this exact one-month gap trap.
Do not skip recently instituted days like **National Space Day (August 23)** and **Veer Baal Diwas (December 26)** as examiners favor current affairs-linked static GK.

items.term: Mistake 4: Mixing Constitution Day and Republic Day
items.definition: Constitution Day is November 26 (**Samvidhan Divas**), whereas Republic Day is January 26 (**Gatantantra Diwas**).

items.term: Mistake 5: Earth Day vs Environment Day
items.definition: Earth Day is April 22, while World Environment Day is June 5. Do not interchange their dates.
National & International Days form a high-scoring component under General Awareness in UPSSSC PET.
**World Water Day (March 22)**, **Earth Day (April 22)**, **Environment Day (June 5)**, and **Ozone Day (September 16)** are exam favorites.
**World Health Day (April 7)**, **AIDS Day (December 1)**, and **Human Rights Day (December 10)** are globally significant UN days.
**Youth Day (Jan 12)**, **Sports Day (Aug 29)**, **Teachers Day (Sept 5)**, and **Kisan Diwas (Dec 23)** honor national icons.
**National Space Day (August 23)** and **Veer Baal Diwas (December 26)** are crucial modern additions to the exam syllabus.
**Constitution Day on November 26** marks the adoption of the Indian Constitution in **1949**.
**International Day of Yoga on June 21** was adopted by the UN following India's initiative in **2014-2015**.
Regular monthly revision and memorizing via mnemonics ensure 100% accuracy in the PET examination.

upscNotes.content: Focus heavily on months with multiple major events like March, April, August, and December, as UPSSSC PET examiners pick questions directly from these clusters.
Always correlate national days with the birth anniversaries of prominent historical personalities as asked in previous UPSSSC exams.
Watch out for matching questions where options deliberately swap National Teachers Day (Sept 5) with World Teachers Day (Oct 5).
Do not confuse the establishment year of international bodies (like WHO in 1948, UN in 1945) with the dates their respective days are observed.

keyTakeaways: Master core recurring dates: Yoga Day, Environment Day, Earth Day, and Water Day.
Distinguish clearly between National and International variants (e.g., Youth Day, Teachers Day).
Keep updated with newly declared national days like Space Day and Veer Baal Diwas.
Use chronological sequencing and mnemonics for seamless recall during the exam.
Revise constitutional and historical milestone dates like Constitution Day and Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.
